title: TrackFlow Telemetry Events
description: JSON Schema definitions for all TrackFlow telemetry events. Each event_type has its own schema under 'definitions'. The EventEnvelope defines the common wrapper fields. Additional properties are forbidden at every level to prevent accidental data leaks.

EventEnvelope.description: Standard wrapper for every telemetry event emitted by TrackFlow systems.

eventId.description: Globally unique identifier for this event, generated at the emission point.

sessionId.description: Identifies the user session. Correlates events within a single login session.

userId.description: UUID of the authenticated user. Use 'anonymous' for events triggered before authentication (e.g. login_attempt).

event_type.description: Event name following the entity_action taxonomy (e.g. inbound_order_created). Must match exactly one definition key.

schemaVersion.description: Semver version of the properties schema. Allows schema evolution without breaking consumers.

requestId.description: HTTP request correlation ID (trace ID). Enables end-to-end tracing across API gateway, service, and database.

properties.description: Event-specific payload. The allowlist of allowed keys is defined per event_type. No extra keys are permitted.

inbound_order_created.description: A warehouse registers receipt of merchandise from a client. Triggered after POST /inventory/orders/inbound. Hypothesis: we need to know inbound volume by client and warehouse. Decision: plan warehouse capacity and staffing (Ana).

client_id.description: B2B client identifier (the brand that owns the SKU).

product_id.description: SKU code of the received product (e.g. CLT-SNK-W-42).

product_category.description: Product category as defined in TrackFlow's SKU model.

reference.description: Inbound order reference (PO number or GR number).

sensitive.notes: No PII. Warehouse inventory data only.

outbound_order_created.description: A warehouse completes picking and dispatch of an order. Triggered after POST /inventory/orders/outbound. Hypothesis: we need to know how many orders are processed per client and warehouse. Decision: detect operational bottlenecks before they affect delivery SLA (Ana).

product_id.description: SKU code of the dispatched product.

exit_type.description: Type of exit: dispatch (normal shipment) or loss (shrinkage/write-off).

sensitive.notes: No PII. Does not include carrier or end-recipient data.

stock_threshold_triggered.description: SKU stock falls below the minimum threshold configured for that client. Evaluated after every outbound_order_created. Hypothesis: we need to know how often a client runs out of stock for a SKU. Decision: alert the client and commercial team before stockout (Miguel).

warehouse.description: Warehouse where the threshold was triggered.

quantity.description: Remaining stock units when the alert fired.

threshold_value.description: Minimum threshold configured for this client/SKU.

current_stock.description: Current stock level after the triggering operation.

sensitive.notes: No PII. Inventory threshold data only.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: A user attempted to modify stock directly (outside an inbound/outbound order) and the system rejected it. Hypothesis: we need to know if warehouse staff tries to bypass traceability controls. Decision: reinforce training or permissions at the warehouse where this occurs most frequently.

warehouse.description: Warehouse targeted by the direct edit attempt.

client_id.description: Client associated with the target SKU.

user_role.description: Role of the user who made the attempt (admin, manager, user).

attempt_type.description: How the direct edit was attempted.

sensitive.notes: No PII. Only user role is recorded, not email or name.

inventory_discrepancy_detected.description: A physical count or audit detected a difference between system stock and actual stock. Hypothesis: we need to know which SKUs and warehouses have the most discrepancies. Decision: prioritize inventory audits on SKUs with the highest discrepancy rate (Ana).

warehouse.description: Warehouse where the discrepancy was found.

client_id.description: Client associated with the discrepant SKU.

expected_quantity.description: Stock quantity recorded in the system.

actual_quantity.description: Actual stock quantity from physical count.

variance.description: Difference: actual - expected. Negative if stock is missing, positive if surplus.

login_succeeded.description: A user successfully logs in. Triggered after POST /auth/login returns 200. Hypothesis: we need to know which users access the system and from which timezone. Decision: detect anomalous access patterns (e.g. Zaragoza operator logging in from a US timezone).

user_id.description: UUID of the authenticated user. Not PII by itself.

ip_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code derived from the request IP (e.g. US, ES). Not the raw IP.

sensitive.notes: IP is reduced to country only. No email, no full IP.

login_failed.description: A login attempt failed due to invalid credentials or inactive user. Hypothesis: we need to detect brute-force patterns. Decision: implement rate-limiting and notify Andres (CTO) on anomalous spikes.

email_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the attempted email. Never the email in plain text.

ip_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code derived from the request IP.

attempt_count_last_5min.description: Number of failed attempts from the same IP in the last 5 minutes.

sensitive.sanitization: Email is SHA-256 hashed before emission. The original email is never included. The full IP is never included, only the country code.
sensitive.retention_policy: email_hash may be retained for 90 days for anomaly detection, then aggregated.

session_token_expired.description: Access to a protected endpoint was rejected because the JWT token has expired. Hypothesis: we need to know how often users encounter expired sessions. Decision: adjust JWT TTL or implement silent refresh tokens.

user_id.description: UUID extracted from the expired token if decodable.

endpoint.description: The API route that was being accessed (e.g. /suppliers).

time_since_login_minutes.description: Minutes elapsed between token issuance and this request.

ip_country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code from the request IP.

sensitive.notes: user_id is a non-reversible UUID. No raw IP.

supplier_created.description: A new supplier was registered in the directory. Triggered after POST /suppliers returns 201. Hypothesis: we need to know how often new suppliers are onboarded and in which market. Decision: anticipate operations workload (Carlos).

rate_per_shipment.description: Rate per shipment in the contract currency.

supplier_rate_updated.description: A supplier's shipment rate was updated. Triggered after PATCH /suppliers/{id}/rate returns 200. Hypothesis: we need to track rate evolution per carrier and market. Decision: renegotiate contracts when a carrier's cumulative increases exceed market average.

updated_by_role.description: Role of the user who performed the update (admin, manager).

supplier_status_toggled.description: A supplier was suspended or reactivated. Triggered after PATCH /suppliers/{id}/status returns 200. Hypothesis: we need to know how often suppliers are suspended/reactivated. Decision: identify carriers with recurring issues before they affect SLA.

incident_created.description: A new operational incident was registered. Triggered after POST /api/incidents returns 201. Hypothesis: we need to know the distribution of incident types by warehouse and country. Decision: allocate preventive resources (e.g. many delivery_failure in LA -> review address quality).

sensitive.notes: description (may contain PII) and title are intentionally excluded from telemetry.

incident_status_changed.description: An incident changed status. Triggered after PATCH /api/incidents/{id}/status returns 200. Hypothesis: we need to measure time between status transitions. Decision: auto-escalate incidents stuck in in_progress for over 24h.

time_in_previous_status_ms.description: Milliseconds the incident remained in the previous status.

updated_by_role.description: Role of the user who changed the status.

api_response_error_recorded.description: The API returned a 4xx or 5xx HTTP error. Emitted from a response middleware. Hypothesis: we need to know the error rate per endpoint. Decision: prioritize fixing the endpoints with the highest error rate.

endpoint.description: API route (without path parameters). E.g. /api/incidents, not /api/incidents/{id}.

error_detail.description: Generic, predefined error description. Never includes user input values, field values, or full stack traces. Examples: 'Validation error', 'Insufficient permissions', 'Resource not found'.

sensitive.notes: error_detail uses only predefined messages. No user input is echoed.

page_navigated.description: A backoffice operator navigated between sections. Emitted from the frontend on route change. Hypothesis: we need to know which sections are most visited and in which order. Decision: reorganize the main navigation to reflect Ana, Carlos, and Valentina's actual workflows.

from_page.description: Source section identifier (e.g. suppliers, incidents_panel, incidents_form).

sensitive.notes: No full URLs with query params. Only logical page names.

lead_form_submitted.description: A website visitor submitted the information request form. Hypothesis: we need to know how many qualified leads the website generates. Decision: evaluate marketing campaign ROI and adjust Miguel's commercial capacity.

product_type.description: Type of product the lead company handles.

operating_country.description: Main operating country of the lead.

has_3pl.description: Whether the lead currently works with another 3PL.

services_interest.description: TrackFlow services the lead is interested in.

sensitive.sanitization: No PII is included: company_name, contact_person, email, phone, website, and comments are all intentionally excluded. Only business profile data is captured.
sensitive.retention_policy: These events are aggregatable and can be retained indefinitely.

cache_effectiveness_recorded.description: Periodic measurement of cache hit/miss for incidents and suppliers endpoints. Hypothesis: we need to know the cache hit rate. Decision: adjust TTLs (currently 60s for incidents, 120s for suppliers) and invalidation strategies.

hit.description: true if served from cache, false if computed.

ttl_seconds.description: Configured TTL for this cache entry.

outbound_order_insufficient_stock.description: An outbound order was rejected because requested quantity exceeds available stock. Hypothesis: we need to know how often operators try to dispatch more stock than available. Decision: adjust minimum thresholds per SKU or review inventory accuracy.

warehouse.description: Warehouse where the insufficient stock was detected.

product_id.description: SKU that could not be dispatched.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the operator tried to dispatch.

available_stock.description: Actual available stock at the time of the request.
